description: Three workload descriptions. Checks look for correct arithmetic on given prices, for hidden cost drivers being counted, for missing prices being left blank, or for a forbidden behaviour such as an invented price. Case-insensitive regular expressions on the final answer.

tasks.prompt: We're adding a customer support chatbot to our SaaS app using a Claude model through the API. We expect about 3,000 conversations a month, 5 back-and-forth turns each. The system prompt with our help-centre content is about 6,000 tokens. Customer messages are short, maybe 60 tokens, and replies are around 200 tokens. Roughly how much will this cost us per month?

checks.why: No prices were given; none may be supplied from memory.
A total needs prices the user has not given.
Missing prices are left blank and requested.
Each turn re-sends the conversation so far.
The 6,000-token system prompt is billed on every turn.
A large static system prompt is the obvious caching candidate.
Gives a low and high case.

tasks.prompt: Can you estimate the monthly cost of our invoice email automation? It processes about 40,000 emails a month. Each email gets one model call that extracts the fields as JSON: about 1,800 input tokens and 150 output tokens per call. Our model costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $6.00 per million output tokens. About 3% of calls fail our JSON check and get re-run once. Results go to Google Sheets and Slack, both on plans we already pay for, so ignore those. Emails have to be processed within a minute of arriving.

checks.why: Shows the token arithmetic.
Gives a low and high case.

checks.pattern: batch[\s\S]{0,200}(not (suitable|an option|possible|fit)|can'?t|cannot|within a minute|24 hours|delay|latency)|(within a minute|latency|delay)[\s\S]{0,200}batch
checks.why: Batch would cut cost but breaks the one-minute requirement; say so.
Only the user's prices (and plainly derived ones) may appear as per-token rates.

tasks.prompt: Estimate the monthly cost of our AI phone receptionist. About 1,200 calls a month, averaging 4 minutes. The voice platform charges $0.05 per minute and our phone carrier $0.01 per minute. Each call has 12 model turns. Every turn sends the 2,500-token system prompt plus the whole conversation so far; each caller utterance is about 150 tokens and each model reply about 60 tokens. The model costs $0.90 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. About 40% of calls end in a booking, and we send the caller a confirmation text message for each booking.

checks.why: Turn k input = 2,650 + (k-1) x 210; 45,660 tokens per call; 54.792M a month; $49.31.
The SMS price was not given and must stay blank.
40% of 1,200 calls = 480 confirmation texts.
No SMS price was given; none may be invented.
Voice minutes, not tokens, drive the bill.
